traits.use — agent & contributor guide

Source: AGENTS.md

traits.use is an R package for loading, exploring and wrangling data from any traits.build relational trait database, such as AusTraits. It began as the austraits package and was split out in 2026 (traitecoevo/austraits#188, history carried over). austraits is becoming a thin AusTraits-specific layer over it. The first CRAN release (0.1.0, maintainer Elizabeth Wenk) is tracked in #13.

Repo-local guidance

  • Code: R/ (functions), tests/ (testthat), man/ (generated docs), NAMESPACE, data-raw/ and inst/ hold raw assets (incl. the cheatsheet); R/sysdata.rda holds the test fixtures.
  • Access entry point: load_database() (R/load_database.R) loads any traits.build database from its doi (Zenodo, Figshare, or a doi resolving directly to an .rds).
  • AusTraits-specific code lives in austraits, not here (decided 2026-11-14, #13): load_austraits(), get_versions() / get_version_latest(), the AusTraits vignette and the map of Australia. plot_locations() takes a basemap data frame so austraits can pass its map.
  • Wrangle/extract: extract_*() (data/dataset/taxa/trait), join_*() (taxa, methods, contributors, locations, context/location properties), lookup_*(), trait_pivot_longer/wider(), summarise_database(), bind_databases(), flatten_database(), as_wide_table().
  • Build/test (standard R-package workflow): devtools::load_all(), devtools::test(), devtools::check(). The package targets R >= 4.1.0 (it uses |>); tidyverse-style Imports (dplyr, tidyr, purrr, etc.). Lifecycle badge is experimental until the first CRAN release.
  • Default branch: master. Docs/pkgdown site at https://traitecoevo.github.io/traits.use/.
  • CRAN-bound: traits.use must never Import/Depend on traits.build (not on CRAN, and +57 recursive dependencies). Keep network tests behind skip_on_cran() / skip_if_offline().

Heads-up: traits.use (like austraits before it) is the downstream access/wrangle layer in the data pipeline, but the R-package install graph runs the other way — traits.build currently Imports austraits (moving to traits.use, see austraits#188) and re-exports a few conversion helpers from it (convert_df_to_list, convert_list_to_df1, convert_list_to_df2, bind_databases, flatten_database — all in NAMESPACE). Changing those helpers can break traits.build; run its tests after touching them.

Heads-up: from Sept 2024 the code works against any traits.build database (not just austraits.build). austraits.build versions < 5.0 are unsupported by the current package — older builds need an older tagged austraits (e.g. traitecoevo/austraits@v2.2.2).

AusTraits family — cross-package context

traits.use is part of the AusTraits family (a subset of the traitecoevo org) — here, the user-facing access/wrangle API (R package) for traits.build-format databases, including AusTraits; loads the released .rds via load_database(). Family-wide concerns are documented centrally in austraits-meta — don’t restate them here, read them there:

  • Start with AGENTS.md — pipeline order, who owns what, dependency direction, source-of-truth rules, cross-boundary artifacts, gotchas.
  • dependencies.yml — machine-readable package graph + cross-boundary artifacts.
  • governance/ — label taxonomy, board #9 conventions, release playbooks, triage.

Filing issues: the whole family is tracked on one board, AusTraits #9 (new issues auto-add to it). Follow the issue & labelling guide: pick one work-type label (bug / task / epic); Status and Priority are set on the board, not as labels.

Commit messages: every family repo squash-merges, so the PR title and body become the permanent commit message. Keep the subject ≤50 characters as typed and the body ≤10 lines; put the working detail — what you tried, benchmarks, test counts, rejected alternatives — in the first PR comment instead. Full convention: commit-messages.md.

austraits-meta is hand-maintained prose — a map, not ground truth. Verify specifics against the actual repos.
